turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My contract ends next month and I need to pick a new phone plan.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll tell you all the choices first. Wait until I'm finished before you comment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a cheap prepaid plan, ten gigs of data, no contract, but the coverage at my parents' place is patchy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My current carrier offered unlimited data for a bit more each month if I sign up for two years.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A family plan with my sister would split the cost, though I'd be tied to her paying on time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's everything. Which one would you pick?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If you use a lot of data, your carrier's unlimited deal is the safe pick, even with the two-year lock. The prepaid plan wins on flexibility, and the family split saves money but mixes in family politics.
